top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on one clean physical idea, the magic-wavelength condition that makes the trap drop out of the measurement, and Ye's group took it to the 10^-18 regime. It has been reproduced and surpassed independently at several laboratories and already yields physics (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, constants and dark-matter bounds). The two-name allocation (Katori, Ye) was proposed identically by all eight members, and the citation scoped to the invention and its 10^-18 performance stays distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. The attribution gap to Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and others is real but cannot be closed under a three-person limit, and it does not justify no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the clock is outside superconducting circuits, though WACQT directorship and Chalmers links to quantum technology are noted generally
